### **Job Description and Duties**

The Fish Restoration Program (FRP) is seeking two creative, curious, and collaborative scientists to help drive cutting edge ecological analysis, interagency coordination, and field based discovery related to tidal wetland restoration across the upper San Francisco Estuary. If you’re excited by the intersection of advanced analytics, restoration science, mentorship, and hands on fieldwork, this is your opportunity to make a direct impact on the future of California’s wetlands.

What You’ll Do

• Lead advanced ecological analyses to evaluate restoration effectiveness and guide adaptive management.

• Synthesize literature, data, and multi program findings into high quality technical reports and peer-reviewed articles.

• Mentor colleagues in data analysis, visualization, and effective scientific communication.

• Work closely with partner agencies to integrate monitoring and synthesis efforts and support responsible data access and use.

• Get outside—conduct boat-based sampling of wetland invertebrates and fishes in and around the eleven FRP restoration projects.

• Support lab operations by sorting invertebrate samples, preparing nutrient samples, and calibrating water quality instruments.

Who You Are

You’re a scientist who enjoys the entire process of transforming samples into knowledge – getting muddy, wrangling data, and communicating findings, while teaching others along the way. You thrive in collaborative, interdisciplinary environments and believe science should be transparent, rigorous, and accessible.

Why This Role Matters

FRP’s monitoring and synthesis will shape California’s wetland restoration planning and management for years to come. Your work will help determine what’s working, why it’s working, and how restoration can be improved to support fish and wildlife in a changing estuary.

Ready to put your analytical, ecological, and communication talents to work for one of the state’s most impactful restoration programs?

Apply today and help build a healthier estuary for future generations.

**Senior Environmental Scientist**

**Perth, WA | Permanent, Full-time / Part-time**

RPS, a Tetra Tech company, is a leading global professional services consultancy delivering solutions across the environment, infrastructure, energy and urban development sectors.

In Australia Asia Pacific, we work with industry, government and communities to define, design and manage complex projects that create shared value. Our people combine technical expertise with practical thinking to help clients understand environmental risks, navigate complex challenges and deliver successful project outcomes.

As part of Tetra Tech, we are connected to a global network of approximately 30,000 employees, providing access to specialist expertise, opportunities and projects across Australia and internationally.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking a Senior Scientist to join our Oceans & Environment team in Perth, or Margaret River. RPS understand the importance of flexible working arrangements and this role is open to both full-time and part-time hours.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early to mid career environmental scientist who has experience in environmental approvals and is looking to continue developing their technical and consulting capability. Working alongside experienced environmental professionals, you will contribute to a range of projects.

**What you'll be involved in**

Your responsibilities will include:

* Preparing environmental approval documentation under the EP Act and EPBC Act.
* Preparing practical environmental management plans and strategies.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Manage multiple tasks on a range of projects and effectively deal with conflicting priorities and work to tight deadlines.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and work co-operatively with people at all levels to achieve outcomes.
* Communicate and maintain good relationships with internal stakeholders, clients, suppliers and project stakeholders.

**About you**

We are looking for someone who is technically curious, practical and keen to build a career in environmental approvals and environmental consulting.

**You will ideally bring:**

* A relevant tertiary qualification in environmental management or environmental science.
* Experience in undertaking environmental impact assessments in Western Australia.
* Understanding of State and Commonwealth environmental legislation, policy and guidance.
* Good technical report writing skills and attention to detail
* Minimum of five years relevant work experience.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* The ability to work independently while knowing when to seek technical guidance
* An understanding of project delivery including quality, safety, time and budget considerations
* A commitment to ongoing professional and technical development

**Why RPS?**

Joining RPS means becoming part of a collaborative environmental team while also having access to the technical capability and opportunities of the broader Tetra Tech network.

You will have the opportunity to develop your career alongside experienced contaminated land specialists, gain exposure to a diverse range of projects and progressively take on greater technical, project and client responsibilities.

**We also offer:**

* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate
* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* Paid professional memberships
* Active lifestyle and wellbeing initiatives
* Employee assistance and wellbeing support
* Opportunities to work with technical specialists across Australia and the wider Tetra Tech network
* A supportive and collaborative team environment
* Paid parental leave and other employee benefits

**Our commitment**

RPS is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people are respected, supported and encouraged to bring their individual perspectives and experience to work.

If you have a foundation in environmental science or contaminated land and are looking for an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while working alongside experienced specialists, we'd like to hear from you.

**Our Approach**

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  
Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.

**APPOINTMENT TYPE:** Temporary Exempt: This position is excluded by the Charter from the competitive Civil Service examination process and shall serve at the discretion of the Appointing Officer. The duration of the appointment shall not exceed 36 months.

**WHO ARE WE?**  
San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)  
Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

**Our Mission:** To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

**Our Vision:** We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site at https://www.sfpuc.org/about-us/careers-sfpuc

**Why Join Us?**

This role offers a unique opportunity to help build and scale up critical water quality initiatives, combining technical analysis, project coordination, and field operations to protect public health across San Francisco and regional water systems. If you are passionate about water quality, regulatory compliance, large-scale infrastructure programs, and building efficient operational processes, we encourage you to apply!

 **Job Description**

**Project Name:** Hazard Assessment Program

**Project Description:**

Under the State of California’s new cross-connection control regulations, the SFPUC must review all service connections (~180,000+) to properties in San Francisco, as well as the eight other water systems under SFPUC’s control, to evaluate potential hazards to the public drinking water distribution system arising from activities on user premises. In addition, the new regulations require the installation of backflow prevention assemblies on about 4,200 fire service connections. SFPUC has submitted a plan to the State Water Resources Control Board with deadlines for completing hazard assessments by 2049, ensuring backflow prevention assemblies on all dedicated fire services by 2044.

**Position Summary**

Are you a technical professional looking to make a direct impact on public health and water safety on a massive scale? We are seeking a dynamic Utility Specialist to serve as the Technical Program Coordinator for our Water Quality Cross Connection Control (CCC) Program under the direction of the Hazard Assessments Program Manager.

In this vital role, you will contribute to the implementation of SFPUC Cross-Connection Control Program inline with new regulatory requirements established by the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) through the Cross Connection Control Policy Handbook (CCCPH).

You will help shape a high-profile, multi-decade program by developing tracking systems, operational processes, coordinating complex field logistics, and partnering with internal teams, contractors, and external stakeholders across multiple program areas including Hazard Assessments, Fire services upgrades and Regional Compliance.

**Work Location:** 1657 Rollins Road, Burlingame, CA, 94010

**Schedule:** Full-time, Monday – Friday

* This position requires a valid driver’s license.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* **Program Implementation & Compliance:** Develop and implement coordination protocols, workflows, and documentation processes for the CCC Program in compliance with SWRCB CCCPH requirements.
* **Systems & Data Management:** Establish tracking systems, dashboards, and reporting templates to monitor inspections, costs, schedules, and compliance metrics.
* **Research & Analysis:** Conduct research using internal databases, GIS systems, spreadsheets, field reports, and photos to compile baseline data on service connection characteristics and assess cross-connection hazards.
* **Cross-Functional Coordination:** Coordinate daily program activities with field staff, contractors, customers, and other City departments, serving as a liaison to ensure smooth communication, scheduling, and execution.
* **Contractor & Consultant Oversight:** Coordinate with contractors and consultants to ensure field activities align with approved scopes of work, schedules, and Cross Connection Control program requirements.
* **Reporting & Continuous Improvement:** Prepare program reports, dashboards, and documentation for Program Manager review, highlighting trends, risks, and lessons learned while developing procedures, reference materials, and recommendations to improve program effectiveness.

jobs.title: Junior Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Toeroek Associates is a dynamic small business provider of specialty consulting and analysis services to the U.S. Government. Our multi-disciplined environmental staff includes scientific, legal, and engineering experts who support federal and state government entities in compliance, remediation, field services, site assessments, oversight, historical and technical research, litigation, and community engagement. Toeroek offers a collaborative and congenial work environment with a team of passionate staff dedicated to finding solutions to complex problems in the fields of environment, records and knowledge management, and national security.

Toeroek Associates is seeking a junior-level Environmental Analyst to provide support in the Denver, Colorado, Sacramento, California, Dallas, Texas, or Chicago, Illinois areas.

**Summary**

The analyst will work as part of a team to assist EPA and other government agencies with administering environmental regulatory compliance and enforcement programs. Our focus is on cleaning up our communities. The analyst will work on multiple contracts, researching and compiling evidence to characterize contamination and identify potentially responsible parties (PRPs) at hazardous waste sites. Superior research, writing, and analytical skills are essential to this position, as is an interest in helping government agencies enforce their environmental regulations.

**Duties include:**

* Assist in identifying sources of information about PRP operations, including federal, state and local agencies, public libraries, private archives, and map and aerial photography archives
* Conduct research to obtain documents pertinent to PRP historical operations and waste disposal practices, as well as environmental regulatory compliance
* Review information on PRP operations, including responses to EPA information requests, facility inspection reports, sampling and investigation reports, hazardous materials inventories and other documents collected, and identify relevant data for purposes of analyzing Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) liability
* Draft evidence summary reports that present information about PRP operations, chemical usage, disposal practices, and soil and groundwater sampling data
* Review laboratory sampling data results for purposes of extracting and summarizing relevant data from sampling and investigation reports
* Review real property title documents and prepare title reports and tables showing the ownership history of the property
* Conduct corporate research and identify corporate successors (training will be provided)
* Input data and manage databases
* Translate information obtained from research into charts, graphs, maps, and infographics
* Occasional overnight travel may be required

**Education/Experience**

* Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts degree from an accredited university
* Minimum of two years of relevant work experience preferred

**Requirements**

* Hybrid arrangements for Lakewood, CO and Concord, CA.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed, critical, and thoughtful writing and analysis skills
* Knowledge of or experience in environmental information collection, analysis, interpretation and report preparation
* Ability to function as a member of a team and work in a fast-paced environment
* Ability to handle multiple tasks at once and meet deadlines and to adapt quickly and smoothly to changing project requirements
* Proficient in Office 365 and Windows-based applications
* Ability to use software to retrieve, evaluate, and organize information and documents

**Bonus Skills/Certifications**

* Experience with ESRI suite of GIS software is a plus

This position's target hiring rate range is non-exempt, $21.63 to $25.48 per hour, DOQ. This is good faith and a reasonable estimate of the base compensation at the time of posting. Toeroek offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Life, LTD, STD, and 401K.

Toeroek Associates, Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer.

*Toeroek Associates, Inc. maintains the policy of equal employment opportunity (EEO) shall apply to all terms, conditions, and privileges of employment, including hiring, testing, training and development, promotion, transfer, compensation, benefits, educational assistance, termination, layoffs, social and recreational programs, and retirement. Toeroek is committed to making employment decisions based on valid requirements, without regard to age, color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, military or veteran status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other applicable status protected by state or local law.*

*Applicants with disabilities may contact Toeroek Associates, Inc., Human Resources via telephone, fax, e-mail, and other means to request and arrange for accommodations. The program coordinates statewide conservation activities for native wildlife, including those designated as threatened or endangered pursuant to the California Endangered Species Act.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking a Federal
Mine Remediation Lead
to be based out of any of our locations in the western United States (AZ, CA, CO, MT, NM, NV, OR, UT). This is a full-time role.

This is an exciting growth focused opportunity to build and lead a Mine remediation group. The person in this position will support business development, project execution and have the ability to grow and lead a Mine Remediation practice. We are seeking a leader with major project delivery experience and proven ability to build and lead technical teams in implementing Mine remediation projects, specifically under CERCLA. Preferential consideration will be given to experience on US Federal projects and strong regulatory connections.

As an experienced professional in Mine remediation, you will bring specific technical expertise, sophisticated regulatory understanding, leadership skills, and an entrepreneurial spirit along with a keen interest in evolving and growing the business and mentoring staff. Your demonstrated commitment to safety along with a strong operational understanding of safety risks in mining environments, and ability to mentor employees to support a safe work culture will supplement AECOM’s existing safety culture.

Responsibilities will include:

Working closely with AECOM personnel in United States and Canada to develop and implement Mine remedial solutions for clients in the public and private sector that meet regulatory requirements and protect human health and the environment.
Collaboration with, and coordination of, diverse technical teams including hydrologists, hydrogeologists, geochemists, risk assessors, environmental engineers, geotechnical engineers, civil engineers, water treatment specialists, biologists, revegetation, costing specialists, etc. to develop remedial solutions that meet technical and regulatory requirements.
Reviewing technical work plans and cost estimates; interpreting data; conducting remediation/closure technology evaluations and feasibility studies.
Technical and financial management of projects to meet commitments on budget, quality and schedule.
Development of proposals, project teams and cost estimates.
Delivery of projects, and technical review of reports for regulatory submission (e.g., studies, remediation and closure plans, permit applications, management plans).
Periodically attending site visits to proposed, operating or closed mines in support of client relationship building, proposal development and project delivery.
Business-development activities, including building and maintaining existing and new client relationships, tracking marketing leads and project opportunities, developing proposals and presentations, networking, attending conferences and sharing AECOM’s capabilities with existing and potential clients.
Stakeholder communications, including regulatory communications and client advocacy.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in relevant engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Environmental etc.) or science (geology, hydrogeology, environmental etc.) disciplines +8 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or 20+ years of experience
People management experience
Mine remediation experience under CERCLA framework
Proficient technical writing experience for investigation and design reports and regulatory document submissions
Proficient proposals preparation and cost development experience for Mine remediation projects
Experience with US Federal projects, specifically with US Army Corps of Engineers, US Environmental Project Agency, US Department of Interior

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $160000 to $210000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Senior Agrochemical Regulatory Affairs Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Inviting bright minds

Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world. Ramboll Health Science Spearhead has approx. 360 bright minds globally and you can become one of them in our Australia team contributing to our continued success.

You will join our Environment and Health Business Unit

As our new Senior Consultant, you will have experience and be a subject matter expert in Agrochemical regulations in Australia (APVMA) and New Zealand (EPA and ACVM). You will bring the ability to organize, coordinate and communicate across an interdisciplinary team, engaging externally with technical professionals, and regulatory agencies. You will provide strategic expertise and support the preparation of regulatory submissions for a variety of agrochemical related products in the region. A strong customer service ethic and ability to multitask is vital for this role. You will present a positive “can-do” attitude and be a self-starter within a team of dedicated professionals.

This is a unique opportunity to have a role within the Ramboll Health Science Spearhead to help drive the growth of the agrochemical consulting business in Australia, working with our international team of regulatory and technical experts, while advancing your skills and consulting career. Reporting to the Principal, Health Sciences in Australia your role would be based at one of Ramboll’s Australian Offices.

Your key tasks and responsibility will be:

Support the execution of Product Stewardship and Safety projects with a focus on Australian and New Zealand plant protection registrations
Act as project manager for interdisciplinary agrochemical regulatory projects
Responsible for strategic guidance and translating complex scientific information into regulator-ready submissions.
Advise clients on existing as well as upcoming regulatory obligations (in the fields of environmental, health & safety-related topics)
Developing strategies, market analysis and helping to expand and drive the growth of Ramboll’s agrochemical business in the region.
Active in business development, meeting clients and attending appropriate conferences and seminars to increase Ramboll’s visibility in the region.

Your starting point for constant growth

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional developments so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

Ability to provide strategic advice and determine practical compliance solutions to meet our clients’ commercial aims for their agricultural related products.
Experience leading multi-faceted teams on projects, producing a high-quality work product, on time and within budget
Ability to guide clients through registrations, variations, and label/claims strategies, helping to prepare compliance advice, application dossiers and data-gap analyses.
Staying current with changes in regulatory landscape affecting Ramboll’s clients and maintaining contacts and relationships with regulatory authorities.
Proficiency assessing the impact of new regional regulations on the business and participates in actions to assist our clients in dealing with the implementation of these new regulations.
Strong team player and customer-oriented approach.

Qualifications

Desired skills/experience

A minimum of 7 years’ industry or consulting experience with plant protection product registration in Australia and New Zealand
Scientific background preferably with a degree or higher in agriculture, veterinary medicine, chemistry, biology or a related discipline
Ability to handle multiple tasks and work streams in a fast-paced environment while maintaining outstanding attention to detail and quality of deliverables
Experience/comfort with working in a virtual team with stakeholders across geographies
Ability to support internal and external clients with both technical and strategic consulting services
Experience in business development would be advantageous
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good presentation skills and business sense
Demonstrated problem-solving skills
Possess a drive and personal initiative to keep learning and improving in the chosen field.

Additional Information

Welcome to our Environment & Health division

Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase livability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll has close to 500 experts working across more than 10 offices in Asia Pacific. We are present in Australia, China, Hong Kong SAR, Malaysia, India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore. Our experts are applying their passion to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions in markets as diverse as Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy and Architecture &, Landscape. Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a people company. We invite you to contribute to a sustainable future working in an open, collaborative and empowering culture.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in Asia Pacific has close to 500 people working across ten offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, and Architecture & Landscape.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist Consultant - January Start
jobs.description:
**About Us**
============

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

**A Day in the Life**
=====================

Formerly known as Epic Environmental, the Australian arm of Onterris has kept the strong culture we are well known for. The team continues to work closely with clients, building trusted relationships and delivering high-quality outcomes without an overemphasis on KPIs.

Our teams have the opportunity to work alongside industry leaders, auditors, and professionals with vast experience within our industry, while enjoying regular social events and collaborative work that bring the team together. Onterris also supports career development through relevant internal opportunities and individual one-on-one career conversations focused on growth and progression.

We are seeking a Consultant Environmental Scientist to join our growing Contaminated Land and Water team out of our Sydney office. Have the opportunity to work alongside more than 50 land and water professionals across Australia who are actively invested in mentoring, collaboration and your long-term career development.

This role will be responsible for a full range of activities including:

* Planning and delivering field investigations across a variety of sites – including soil, groundwater, and surface water assessments

* Preparing clear and high-quality reports

* Acting as the representative/client contact on site for Onterris

* Attending business development meetings

Supporting project managers and ensuring open and clear communications when in the field  



**Your Expertise and Skills**
=============================

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

* 1-3 years consulting experience in contaminated land

* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or related disciplines

* Solid understanding of NSW and national environmental frameworks

* Confidence in the field and an eye for detail and technical excellence

* Open C class drivers licence valid in NSW

Onterris is a leading global environmental solutions company partnering with organizations to solve complex challenges where environmental pressures, regulatory expectations and operational risks intersect. Guided by our mission to advance the way of life without compromising the integrity of our environment, we believe environmental responsibility and human progress are fundamentally connected. Our scientists, engineers, field teams and consultants apply systems thinking that unites science, data and practical expertise to deliver solutions that strengthen our clients’ resilience, mitigate risk and protect the air, water and soil that sustain communities, while uncovering responsible paths forward for planet and progress. For more information, visit www.onterris.com .

We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We acknowledge that these experiences and perspectives help to enrich our teams and contribute to our ongoing success. We are committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation in our employment for all applicants. For US residents, click here to learn more.

Full-time | Permanent Position

jobs.title: Associate Director / Director, Nonclinical Toxicology
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Associate Director or Director of Toxicology
to join our nonclinical development team to support discovery and development programs, with a primary focus on nonclinical study oversight and toxicology. The primary focus of this role is to act as a key scientific and operational interface with external contract research organizations (CROs). The individual in this role will assume primary responsibility for the planning, execution, and monitoring of nonclinical studies, ensuring scientific rigor, data quality, and alignment with program timelines and regulatory expectations. This position requires strong scientific judgment, knowledge of regulatory guidance, effective communication, and the ability to independently manage multiple studies in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. This role will also contribute to the preparation of nonclinical components of regulatory dossiers related documentation.
This individual will also serve as a scientific and strategic partner to cross-functional project teams, driving the design, execution, and interpretation of nonclinical toxicology studies in support of IND-enabling and lifecycle safety assessment programs. The role requires close collaboration with internal stakeholders (project leaders, DMPK, regulatory affairs, clinical development) as well as direct oversight of external Contract Research Organizations (CROs) conducting GLP and non-GLP toxicology studies.
This is a hands-on, operationally-focused role: the ideal candidate pairs strong scientific judgment with the rigor to keep multiple CRO-run studies on schedule, on budget, and audit-ready.
The level of hire (Associate Director vs. Director) will be determined based on the candidate's experience, scope of responsibility, and demonstrated leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Author, review, and finalize toxicology study protocols, amendments, and study reports in collaboration with CRO partners, ensuring scientific rigor and regulatory compliance.
Interface directly with CROs to scope, place, monitor, and troubleshoot in-life toxicology studies (GMP and non-GMP), including dose range-finding, repeat-dose, safety pharmacology, and specialized studies as needed.
Serve as Study Monitor for in-life toxicology studies, including on-site or virtual monitoring visits, real-time issue resolution, and direct follow-up with CRO study directors to keep studies on track.
Own budget tracking and oversight for assigned studies — reviewing CRO quotes and change orders, monitoring spend against forecast, and flagging deviations to project teams and finance.
Review and interpret toxicology data (clinical pathology, histopathology, TK/PK) to assess safety signals and inform risk assessment and dose selection.
Author and contribute toxicology sections for IND (or CTA) submissions, Investigator's Brochures, and briefing documents; support preparation of responses to health authority questions.
Partner with DMPK, pharmacology, CMC, and clinical teams to integrate toxicology findings into overall program risk/benefit assessments.
Track study timelines, budgets, and deliverables across multiple concurrent CRO-run studies; escalate risks and resolve issues proactively.
Stay current with regulatory guidance (FDA, ICH, EMA) and industry best practices in toxicology and nonclinical safety assessment.
Serve as toxicology representative and strategic partner on multidisciplinary project teams, providing scientific input on nonclinical safety strategy from discovery through IND/CTA filing and beyond.

Required Qualifications
S., M.S., Ph.D., DVM, or advanced degree in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Veterinary Medicine, or a related biomedical science (or equivalent experience).
5–10 years of relevant experience in toxicology within pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO settings.
Demonstrated experience writing and reviewing toxicology study plans/protocols and final study reports.
Direct experience managing or interfacing with CROs conducting in-life toxicology studies.
Experience serving as Study Monitor on GMP toxicology studies, including in-life visits, protocol/report review, and direct communication with CRO study directors.
Working knowledge of study budgets — able to review CRO quotes/change orders, track spend against budget, and flag scope or cost deviations to project teams.
Solid understanding of GMP regulations, ICH guidelines (e.g., M3(R2), S9, S6), and FDA/EMA nonclinical safety expectations.
Demonstrated experience contributing toxicology content to IND submissions (or CTA equivalent), including authoring nonclinical written summaries and supporting health authority interactions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey complex scientific concepts to cross-functional and non-toxicology audiences.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects and timelines in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
DABT (Diplomate, American Board of Toxicology) certification strongly recommended.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience across multiple modalities (small molecule, biologics, ADCs) preferred but not required.
Prior experience in a sponsor-side role managing external vendor relationships.
Experience presenting toxicology data to internal governance committees or health authorities.
Experience with Veeva or other document management systems.

jobs.description:

Advance Airport Development
Transform the Customer Experience
Optimize Ongoing Business
Cultivate Our Culture

Here, culture starts with each of us. Our workplace is shaped by mindsets that guide how we show up for one another: believing the best in people, collaboration, empathy, listening, and thoughtful decision-making. If you are ready to contribute to a team that values meaningful impact and enjoys the journey along the way, we invite you to apply today and help us connect our community to the world.

Why You'll Love Working At SAN

Location: The new Airport Authority Administration building, located on the San Diego International Airport campus and near the waterfront, providing stunning views of our runway, San Diego Bay, the Pacific Ocean, and the city skyline.
Hybrid Schedule: This role follows a hybrid schedule with both on-site and remote work. On-site days are required, based on department needs, to support collaboration and business operations. Remote work flexibility is available on other days as determined by the department.
Salary: The hiring salary for Associate Environmental Specialist is starting at $100,885-$116,018 The full pay range for Associate Environmental Specialist is $77,604-$124,167.
Benefits: You will enjoy 14 paid holidays, 18 – 33 days of vacation (PTO), parental and child care benefits, salary continuance for family & parental leave, tuition reimbursement, ensure your future with our retirement plan options including our comprehensive pension plan and 457 defined contribution plan. Plus, take advantage of our annual employer-funded Lifestyle Spending Account, designed to support your personal development and growth activities—and much more!
Wellness: Enjoy a workplace that makes well‑being part of the daily routine! Tap into multiple on‑site gyms, unwind or brainstorm in outdoor workspaces, connect with financial wellness advisors, and explore scenic walking trails just steps from campus, all wrapped in a supportive wellness package designed to help you feel your best inside and outside of work.
Application Deadline: October 20, 2026. Applications will be reviewed after the closing date.

About The Job

The Planning, Noise, & Environment Department is seeking an Associate Environmental Specialist
who is passionate about environmental protection and has a knack for building strong, positive relationships across diverse teams. In this role, you'll play a crucial part in ensuring storm water compliance throughout the entire lifecycle of construction projects at the airport, from design to post-construction. You’ll be responsible for reviewing project plans, attending meetings, performing inspections, and ensuring that environmental standards are met in real-time, making this role a blend of fieldwork and public administration. A minimum of three days in the office is required for this position.

The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of environmental regulations [California Construction General Permit, Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) permit, California Industrial General Permit, dewatering discharge permits] and a proactive approach to risk mitigation. The ideal candidate is able to connect with a wide range of stakeholders—from construction crews, regulatory agencies, tenants, and contractors. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the airport’s sustainability goals while building lasting relationships and ensuring that complex environmental challenges are addressed effectively and collaboratively.

What You’ll Do

Ensure Environmental Compliance for Construction Projects: Review project plans for capital, tenant improvement, and major maintenance projects, attend pre-design and pre-construction meetings, review field design changes, and monitor construction to ensure adherence to environmental regulations and organizational initiatives.
Mitigate Environmental Risks: Participate in technical processes, compliance audits, reporting, and permitting activities to minimize environmental impact before and during construction projects.
Support the Authority’s Stormwater Program: Conduct field inspections, coordinate with contractors to meet compliance requirements, and review stormwater data and lab reports.
Collaborate with Stakeholders: Partner with internal teams, regulatory agencies, contractors, and tenants on environmental program issues, inspections, trainings, and incident management.
Track projects: monitor construction projects throughout their lifecycle, identify environmental considerations, and facilitate coordination and communication between departments.
Support Sustainability Programs: Contributeto the development, implementation, and tracking of sustainability initiatives, working with various stakeholders to drive progress.
Develop Environmental Reports and Documentation: Write and maintain documents, reports, records, and operating procedures related to environmental regulations, ensuring accuracy and compliance.
Participate in Environmental Training and Outreach: Lead or assist in educational activities, promotional events, and outreach efforts related to environmental programs and sustainability initiatives.
Work-Related Driving*: Regular driving of Authority vehicles to access construction sites and other locations throughout Airport Authority property for inspections, monitoring, meetings, and other environmental program activities.

The Skills You Need

Business Process Knowledge - Identifies, documents, and monitors processes and develops framework for processes and improvement.
Communication - Proficiently exchanges information through various avenues including verbal, digital, written, facilitation, and persuasion.
Critical Thinking - Critically reviews and translates requirements, data, and information to specify solutions or alternative practice in support of organizational objectives and strategies.
Problem-Solving/Agility - Analyzes situations or factors and collaboratively generates alternatives or solutions, readily adapts behavior or new work methods to evolving and unexpected situations.
Relationship Building- Builds and maintains relations with stakeholders, identifies and relates information, ideas and problems, champions initiatives and ideas based on mutually acceptable solutions.
Leveraging Technology - Uses electronic information and systems effectively.
Planning & Execution - Ability to plan, organize, and execute projects from start to finish. Creates momentum within projects for the benefit of the team; can turn ideas into actions.

About The Team

The Planning, Noise, and Environment (PNE) department helps shape what comes next for SAN. The department brings a long-range perspective on how the airport grows, operates, and connects with the surrounding region with work spanning airport and regional planning, land use, noise, and environmental programs. PNE works across disciplines and alongside teams throughout the Airport Authority, serving as thoughtful stewards of the different perspectives, priorities, and interests that shape complex initiatives.

Within PNE, the Environment team is a group of approximately eight professionals dedicated to integrating sustainability and environmental compliance into how SAN plans for, develops, and operates the airport. The team leads initiatives related to water stewardship, strategic energy, carbon neutrality, clean transportation, biodiversity, zero waste, and climate resilience. To advance these efforts, staff collaborate with teams across the Airport Authority, as well as tenants, contractors, construction crews, external agencies, and regional partners.

Requirements

The Experience You Need to Have**:

Four years of increasingly responsible experience involving analysis, planning, and/or implementation of professional environmental-related program assignments, or any equivalent combination of education, training, or experience.
Graduation from an accredited four-year college or university with a major in environmental science, public or business administration, or a closely related field.

Licenses, Certificates, And Special Requirements

Maintain a valid driver’s license and the ability to maintain insurability under the Authority’s vehicle insurance policy.

Preferred Licenses; Certificates; Special Requirements:

Current Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD), Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP), and/or Qualified Industrial Stormwater Practitioner (QISP) certification, LEED Green Associate and/or LEED AP credential.
Experience supporting construction projects and/or experience working within or in partnership with a public agency.
Driving is an Essential Function

This role requires regular driving as a critical part of performing work-related duties, specifically involving the operation of Airport Authority vehicles. A valid California driver’s license is required, along with strict adherence to all traffic laws and safety regulations. Applicants must maintain an acceptable driving record to operate Authority vehicles. Compliance with Airport Authority vehicle use policies, including safety protocols and reporting requirements, is mandatory. Applicants must acknowledge that driving Airport Authority vehicles is an essential function of this role.

Don’t meet every requirement? That’s okay. At San Diego International Airport, we value your unique experience and your willingness to learn. Some roles require specific qualifications or degrees, but others don’t—and we're always open to individuals committed to growth and excellence. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply. Working closely with AECOM personnel in United States and Internationally to develop and implement Mine remedial solutions for clients in the public and private sector that meet regulatory requirements and protect human health and the environment.

Delivery of projects, and technical review of reports for regulatory submission (e.g., studies, remediation and closure plans, permit applications, management plans).
Periodically attending site visits to proposed, operating or closed mines in support of client relationship building, proposal development and project delivery.
Business-development activities, including building and maintaining existing and new client relationships, tracking marketing leads and project opportunities, developing proposals and presentations, networking, attending conferences and sharing AECOM’s capabilities with existing and potential clients.
Stakeholder communications, including regulatory communications and client advocacy

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in relevant engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Environmental etc.) or science (geology, hydrogeology, environmental etc.) disciplines +10 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education, including 2 years of leadership
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or 20+ years of experience
People management experience
Experience managing complex environmental consulting or Engineering, Procurement, and Construction Management (EPCM) projects
Experience with remediation under CERCLA and RCRA frameworks
Proficient technical writing experience for investigation and design reports and regulatory document submissions
Proficient proposals preparation and cost development experience for Mine remediation projects
Some experience with NEPA, CWA, and NPDES permitting
Experience working on projects for mining companies
Experience with US Federal projects, specifically with US Army Corps of Engineers, US Environmental Project Agency, US Department of Interior

jobs.description:
About Us:

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview:

TRC is seeking a motivated junior-level Environmental Scientist to join our Engineering, Construction, and Remediation practice in Concord, CA. The position focuses on a candidate seeking to develop technical skills to support various environmental consulting services.

This role will primarily assist with field inspections, documentation, reporting, coordination, and other compliance activities related to stormwater management programs. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of senior managers, integrate with our diverse regional team, and demonstrate flexibility and motivation to support various field and technical efforts.

  
Responsibilities:

* Conduct stormwater inspections at construction, industrial, and municipal sites.
* Assist with compliance evaluations related to stormwater permits and environmental regulations.
* Document field observations, site conditions, and potential compliance issues.
* Collect stormwater-related field data and support sampling activities.
* Prepare inspection reports, compliance documentation, and technical summaries.
* Maintain accurate records of inspections, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.
* Support development and implementation of Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Linear Construction Activity Notifications (LCANs) and related compliance documents.
* Assist in identifying BMP recommendations and corrective actions and tracking resolution of deficiencies.
* Perform other compliance inspections, including Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) and tank inspections.
* Perform additional environmental field services and office-based tasks to assist with non-stormwater projects, including environmental investigations, remedial actions, construction monitoring, technical evaluations, compliance programs, and proposals.
* Perform environmental sampling (for soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil gas, and indoor air) in accordance with state and federal regulations, QA/QC procedures, and established standard operating procedures.
* Coordinate with task and project managers, clients, contractors, and regulatory stakeholders as needed.
* Follow health, safety, and quality procedures during field and office work.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Geology, or a related field.
* 1-3 years of relevant experience in stormwater inspection/management, environmental consulting, or related areas.
* Ability to prepare clear and accurate field notes and reports.
* Responsibility and accountability to perform assigned tasks to completion, both independently and working with a team.
* Ability to learn through on-the-job experience and retain knowledge for progressive development.
* Strong problem-solving skills and written and verbal communication.
* Willingness to travel for fieldwork and project assignments (up to approximately 80% local travel). Field activities will require working outdoors in varying weather and site conditions and may include walking on uneven terrain and lifting light equipment.
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Must be able to pass a pre-employment background check, drug screen, physical, and motor vehicle records check.
* Prior experience related to stormwater, erosion and sediment control, field inspections, environmental compliance/permitting requirements, environmental sampling procedures, data analysis, and reporting.
* Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) certification.
* OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification, including current annual refresher.

#LI-SE1

* Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
* 401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.
* Paid time off contingent upon full time or part-time status and level of seniority (ranging from 15 to 25 days per year).
* All full-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.
* TRC ensures that all employees, including those that work part-time, receive paid sick, family, and disability leave in accordance with the laws of their state of residence.

jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**

We are seeking an experienced Team Manager to join our South East Queensland Water Resources team. We welcome candidates with either a Flood Engineering or Drainage Engineering background and approximately 15-20 years of industry experience.

This role combines technical excellence with team leadership. While your primary focus will be technical project delivery, client engagement, and business development, your time will be also dedicated to leading and developing a high-performing team.

You will work closely with the Sector Manager and be supported by People Managers to ensure the team remains technically strong, well-resourced, engaged, and aligned with our growth strategy.

**The Role**

As Team Manager, you will provide senior technical leadership across complex water resources, flood, drainage, and stormwater projects while taking accountability for team performance, capability development, resourcing, and culture.

You will play a key role in ensuring the team is appropriately resourced, equipped with the right skills, and positioned to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients.

**How you’ll make a difference**

* Lead the delivery of complex flood, drainage, and water resources projects.
* Provide technical leadership, mentoring, and quality assurance across project teams.
* Build strong client relationships and support business development opportunities.
* Manage team workload, resourcing, and workshare to achieve business objectives.
* Identify capability gaps and support training, professional development, and succession planning.
* Foster a positive, collaborative, and high-performing team culture.
* Support career development discussions and follow up on development plans.
* Promote effective communication and collaboration across business lines and regions.
* Contribute to sector strategy, pipeline planning, and future resource forecasting.

  
**Qualifications**

The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

**The qualities that help you thrive**

* A strong background in either Flood Engineering or Drainage Engineering (Approximately 13+ years of consulting experience)
* Proven experience leading multidisciplinary teams and mentoring technical professionals.
* Strong commercial awareness, with experience balancing project delivery, and team performance.
* Excellent communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.
* Experience developing client relationships and contributing to business growth.
* CPEng and RPEQ accreditation (or the ability to obtain them).
* Proficiency with industry-standard software such as TUFLOW, RORB, HEC-RAS, DRAINS, 12d, XP-STORM, MUSIC, MIKE Flood, and GIS platforms.
* Sound knowledge of Australian Rainfall and Runoff (ARR), Queensland Urban Drainage Manual (QUDM), TMR Drainage Manual requirements, and relevant Australian Standards and industry guidelines.

  
**Additional Information**

This is an opportunity to help shape the future of one of South East Queensland's leading Water Resources teams. You will continue to work on technically challenging projects while playing a key leadership role in developing people, building capability, and driving team success.

If you are passionate about engineering excellence and leading high-performing teams, we'd love to hear from you.

**Why you’ll love working with us**

* Flexible work arrangements, including alternative start/finish times, job-sharing and hybrid work options
* Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave per year
* Volunteer and representation leave
* Flex public holidays – swap Easter or other holidays for ones that suit you better

**Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?**

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.

Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

About Us:

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview:

TRC is seeking a motivated entry- or junior-level Environmental Scientist to join our Engineering, Construction, and Remediation practice in Rancho Cordova, CA. The position focuses on a candidate seeking to develop technical skills to support various environmental consulting services.

This role will primarily assist with field inspections, documentation, reporting, coordination, and other compliance activities related to stormwater management programs. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of senior managers, integrate with our diverse regional team, and demonstrate flexibility and motivation to support various field and technical efforts.

  
Responsibilities:

* Conduct stormwater inspections at construction, industrial, and municipal sites.
* Assist with compliance evaluations related to stormwater permits and environmental regulations.
* Document field observations, site conditions, and potential compliance issues.
* Collect stormwater-related field data and support sampling activities.
* Prepare inspection reports, compliance documentation, and technical summaries.
* Maintain accurate records of inspections, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.
* Support development and implementation of Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and Linear Construction Activity Notifications (LCANs) and related compliance documents.
* Assist in identifying BMP recommendations and corrective actions and tracking resolution of deficiencies.
* Perform other compliance inspections, including Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) and tank inspections.
* Perform additional environmental field services and office-based tasks to assist with non-stormwater projects, including environmental investigations, remedial actions, construction monitoring, technical evaluations, compliance programs, and proposals.
* Perform environmental sampling (for soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil gas, and indoor air) in accordance with state and federal regulations, QA/QC procedures, and established standard operating procedures.
* Coordinate with task and project managers, clients, contractors, and regulatory stakeholders as needed.
* Follow health, safety, and quality procedures during field and office work.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Geology, or a related field.
* 0-3 years of relevant experience in stormwater inspection/management, environmental consulting, or related areas.
* Ability to prepare clear and accurate field notes and reports.
* Responsibility and accountability to perform assigned tasks to completion, both independently and working with a team.
* Ability to learn through on-the-job experience and retain knowledge for progressive development.
* Strong problem-solving skills and written and verbal communication.
* Willingness to travel for fieldwork and project assignments (up to approximately 80% local travel). Field activities will require working outdoors in varying weather and site conditions and may include walking on uneven terrain and lifting light equipment.
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Must be able to pass a pre-employment background check, drug screen, physical, and motor vehicle records check.
* Prior experience related to stormwater, erosion and sediment control, field inspections, environmental compliance/permitting requirements, environmental sampling procedures, data analysis, and reporting.
* Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) certification.
* OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification, including current annual refresher.

jobs.title: Lead Environmental Specialist/Planner (QSD/QSP)
jobs.description:
About Insignia Environmental

Insignia Environmental (Insignia) is a collaborative, fast-paced growing environmental consulting firm full of bright, motivated employees. Our services are focused on the unique needs of energy projects, including renewables, electricity, and gas. We pride ourselves on being solution-oriented and go beyond traditional environmental review and permitting to leverage innovative concepts and technology to deliver results for our clients. Our reputation in the industry precedes us, and we are extremely proud of it!

Why Join Us?

We love our employees, listen to their input, and strive to take care of them. We are constantly investing in and providing opportunities for development and growth through internal training programs and our professional development program. We frequently gather for team-building events to strengthen our relationships and celebrate our employees’ milestones. We value giving back to our community and hold several volunteer events for our employees every year.

In support of our goal of being the best place to work, Insignia offers a casual, flexible work environment with generous benefits, including a 401(k)-equivalent program, medical insurance (including partial coverage for significant others and dependents), and an above-industry amount of paid time off that escalates with tenure. Our canine friends are also invited to “work” in the office with us!

Position Details

Insignia is seeking a Lead Environmental Specialist/Planner with Qualified SWPPP Developer and Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSD/QSP) certifications to support projects across the Northern California region. This is a full-time, hybrid role that includes regular travel for site visits and field inspections, with occasional overnight stays depending on project location.

Applicants must be based in California. While the preferred reporting locations are our Menlo Park office, we will consider candidates located elsewhere within Northern California who are not within a reasonable commuting distance. In these cases, remote work will be supported for technical and project management tasks when not in the field.

Job Description

Prepare SWPPPs under the State Water Resources Control Board’s General Construction Permit Order 2022-0057-DWQ, including site best management practices maps.
Conduct regular SWPPP inspections, including pre-, during-, and post-rain event assessments, and water quality sampling during storm events.
Coordinate with project personnel, environmental inspectors, and hazardous materials specialists to ensure compliance with water quality mitigation measures.
Manage SWPPP documentation, inspection reports, project changes, equipment logs, and spill logs.
Develop permitting assessments, prepare permit applications, and support compliance management during project construction.
Assist with environmental impact analyses under the California Environmental Quality Act/National Environmental Policy Act (CEQA/NEPA), including preparation of planning documents, environmental review documents, and resource agency permits (e.g., Clean Water Act Section 404/401 and Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements).
Support the completion of environmental deliverables in accordance with approved budgets and schedules.
Participate in internal and client meetings related to project progress and milestones.
Collaborate with peers and provide clients with technical advice and guidance regarding compliance with environmental regulations.
Provide technical review and quality control of environmental assessment documents, permit application packages, technical studies, and related client deliverables.

Requirements

Bachelor of Science degree or higher in hydrology, earth sciences, environmental science, environmental planning, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in environmental consulting, with demonstrated experience in project management support and field inspection roles.
Must hold QSD and QSP certifications.
Additional certifications preferred, including Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control, Professional Engineer, or Professional Geologist.
Working knowledge of regulations pertaining to environmental protection, including CEQA/NEPA, the Clean Water Act, and the Endangered Species Act.
Previous experience participating in the management of projects, including client interaction, technical review of deliverables, schedule, and budget controls.
Demonstrated ability to complete projects on time and within budget.
Excellent communication and organizational skills, as well as confidence in dealing with clients, regulators, and team members.
Ability to exercise informed and independent decision-making.
Excellent writing and technical editing skills, with advanced experience in the Microsoft Office suite.
Rigorously detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy.

Other

Valid driver’s license and good driving record.
Ability to travel as needed for field inspections and project meetings.
Ability to perform physical tasks, including walking/hiking in varying terrain and working in inclement weather conditions.
Ability to lift up to 25 pounds.

Benefits And Compensation

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and location. The annualized salaried range for this position is $70,000 to $95,000.
Insignia is proud to offer a comprehensive benefits program to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Insignia’s benefits include medical, dental, vision, life, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absence, voluntary benefits, employee assistance program, retirement savings plan, and bonuses.

How To Apply

Insignia is committed to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace where every team member can thrive. If you are passionate about making a difference in the environment and want to join a team that values excellence and camaraderie, we would love to hear from you!

Interested applicants should submit a resume with a brief cover letter or cover email. We request that applicants refrain from calling our office directly regarding this position.

Insignia may request, for lawful employment purposes, background information about candidates from a consumer reporting agency in connection with employment.

Insignia is an equal opportunity employer. Insignia does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, childbirth, national origin, age, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, sexual identity, mental or physical disability, genetic predisposition or characteristics, or any other characteristics protected by applicable state or federal civil rights law.
