Serve as a key member of an experienced team of Air SMEs, with opportunities to lead initiatives, broaden technical expertise, and influence environmental strategy. Responsibilities will include the following:

Serving as a trusted advisor to field Environmental Specialists by providing day-to-day air permitting and regulatory compliance support.

Leading and supporting implementation of new and revised air regulations (i.e., 40 CFR Part 60 Subpart XXa and Part 63 Subparts R and BBBBBB).

Collaborating with, and providing support and backup for, other Air SMEs (e.g., storage tanks, CEMS, LDAR), creating opportunities to expand expertise across multiple programs.

Performing and documenting New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) determinations for terminal, pipeline, and marine projects.

Leading and supporting air permit and compliance audits, communicating insights to stakeholders, and driving continuous improvement through the internal auditing program.

Representing L&S in rule advocacy efforts through trade organizations, such as the International Liquid Terminals Association (ILTA), and helping shape practical regulatory outcomes.

Creating and improving guidance documents and compliance tools that establish consistent practices and enable effective decision-making across the organization.

Developing and delivering training to field Environmental Specialists on a wide range of air compliance and permitting topics, strengthening technical capability across the team.

Helping lead emerging technology evaluations and digital transformation initiatives, such as Next Gen Maintenance and the new Environmental Accounting & Tasking system.
Serve as Air Permitting Coordinator for the L&S organization — a visible leadership assignment that connects environmental expertise with engineering, operations, business development, and senior stakeholders.

Represent L&S Environmental in engineering, business development, and other project-related meetings, providing clear recommendations and helping teams navigate permitting and scope decisions.

Own and advance the air permit and project tracking program.

Set air permitting priorities and strategically align internal and external resources.

Identify the timeliest and most cost-effective permitting pathways to support project schedules and business objectives.

Provide clear, proactive project updates — including scope changes and permit timing — to stakeholders and leadership.

Lead or support development of air permit applications, complete detailed reviews of draft permits, and recommend solutions to complex permitting issues.

Build productive relationships with state agencies and Field Environmental Specialists to obtain permits that support business objectives.

Develop into a recognized Air Permitting SME for New Source Review (NSR), Title V (major), and non-Title V (minor) permitting, with a pathway to broader technical and organizational leadership.

Our client is seeking an experienced Environmental Compliance Manager
to support environmental compliance activities across multiple projects and operating facilities throughout California.

This position will combine environmental leadership with hands-on technical compliance responsibilities. The Environmental Compliance Manager will support projects through various stages of development, construction, and operations while working closely with internal project teams, field personnel, consultants, and regulatory agencies.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in environmental permitting and compliance within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or another highly regulated environment. This individual should be comfortable interpreting complex environmental requirements, providing direction to others, managing multiple priorities, and ensuring compliance requirements are effectively implemented in the field.

Responsibilities

Lead and coordinate environmental compliance activities across multiple project and operational sites.
Provide technical guidance and direction to environmental personnel, consultants, contractors, and project teams.
Support environmental compliance throughout pre-construction, construction, and ongoing operations.
Review environmental permits, plans, mitigation measures, and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical field requirements.
Oversee field inspections, compliance documentation, regulatory reporting, corrective actions, and permit obligations.
Support compliance programs involving stormwater and water quality, wildlife and biological resources, spill prevention, air quality, hazardous materials, and waste.
Coordinate with regulatory and resource agencies and support agency inspections, meetings, and compliance responses.
Track environmental commitments, permit conditions, reporting deadlines, corrective actions, and other compliance obligations.
Review environmental reports, field documentation, regulatory submissions, and technical work products.
Coordinate environmental consultants and technical service providers.
Develop practical environmental procedures, training materials, checklists, and field tools.
Identify potential environmental compliance risks and work with internal stakeholders to develop appropriate corrective and preventive actions.
Support environmental permitting and due diligence activities associated with new and existing projects.
Maintain organized and accurate environmental compliance records.
Travel to project and operating sites throughout California as needed.

﻿

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Natural Resources, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
5+ years of progressive environmental compliance experience within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or a comparable environment.
Experience leading environmental programs, projects, field teams, or environmental professionals.
Strong understanding of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience interpreting environmental permits and implementing requirements in active field environments.
Experience with construction and/or operational environmental compliance.
Knowledge of stormwater/SWPPP, spill prevention, hazardous materials and waste, air quality, water quality, and environmental permitting.
Experience with wildlife, biological resources, mitigation monitoring, and resource agency permitting is highly desirable.
Experience interacting with regulatory agencies and environmental consultants.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple sites, deadlines, and priorities.

**Job Overview:**

APTIM is seeking a motivated entry-level Environmental Scientist to support our portfolio of federal environmental investigation and remediation projects. Projects commonly involve the investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by chlorinated solvents, petroleum, radiological contaminants, or emerging compounds. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of project managers and partner with other engineers, scientists, geologists, risk assessors, and health physicists.

**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**

* Assist with the collection, documentation, and organization of field data to support project objectives.
* Contribute to the preparation of project work plans and deliverables.
* Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimates for proposal efforts.
* Develop and maintain spreadsheets, dashboards, and data-tracking tools.
* Assist in the management, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical analysis and data visualization tools.
* Identify and evaluate environmental risks and recommend remediation strategies to support compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Adhere to established health and safety policies and procedures and execute work in a safe and conscientious manner.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science or a related scientific discipline (completed or in progress).
* Relevant internship, research, or academic project experience involving environmental investigation, water or wastewater treatment, sustainability, or ecological conservation (0–2 years).
* Strong interest in environmental remediation, field investigations, treatment systems, and environmental compliance.
* Must have strong written and oral communication skills.
* Willingness to learn field sampling methods, equipment operation, and environmental data collection procedures.
* Ability to perform essential field duties, including walking on uneven terrain, lifting and carrying field equipment, and working outdoors in varying weather conditions.
* Ability to wear and use required PPE.
* Ability to travel to work sites, including overnight travel.
* Valid driver's license.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or authorized to work on federal contracts.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Completion of 40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training.
* Experience using AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, or similar tools) to support technical communication, analytical tasks, research, and efficient project execution. Upon hire, employees are expected to use these tools in accordance with approved company guidelines.

### **Job Description and Duties**

**Per CCR 249.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**

  

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and at milk processing and PRMP plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, collect samples for regulatory surveillance, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairy farms, milk processing plants, bulk milk haulers and other dairy food and PRMP facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard dairy products to California consumers.

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

The duties of this job are performed outdoors approximately 75% of the time. The incumbent reports to the Regional Office only to pick up supplies, attend meetings and turn in required documents. Most of the workday will be spent traveling in a state vehicle to various locations throughout the region.

  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperature, fumes and gases. The noise level in equipment rooms may be high. The incumbent must follow CDFA, Division, and Branch employee health and safety policies, including but not limited to the Respiratory Protection Program.

  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While the CDFA supports telework where possible, in-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

### **Department Information**

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.

  

The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch (MDFS) is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMPs) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. The Branch also responds to food safety incidents, and initiates product impounds and recalls as warranted. Branch personnel provide training and supervision for county Approved Milk Inspection Services and conduct ratings and inspections of farms, processors, and manufacturers of single-service dairy containers for compliance with requirements of the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to ensure approval of California dairy products in interstate commerce. In addition, the Branch ensures that commercial laboratory testing used to determine the basis of payment for milk or for screening of milk for drug residues prior to processing is conducted according to required methods to protect consumers and the marketplace.
